newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Six die in latest Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Six die in latest Colombian violence.

text.p: At least five leftist guerrillas died in clashes with the military in eastern Colombia early on Sunday, military chiefs said.
And in a separate attack in the same region, a left-wing political leader was gunned down outside his home by unidentified assassins, local radio reported.

The five Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels were killed near the town of El Castillo in eastern Meta province. Divisional army commander Gen. Rodolfo Herrera said machine guns, rifles and ammunition were also seized in the counterinsurgency operation.

The fighting was the latest round in a bloody offensive unleashed by the country's three main guerrilla forces six weeks ago, which some military experts say is the most violent phase of combat in more than three decades of armed uprising. More than 150 members of the security forces and civilians have died in the latest phase of conflict.

In Meta's main town, Villavicencio, Josue Giraldo Cardona, a provincial leader of the Marxist-inspired Union Patriotica and a human rights activist was shot dead by two motorcycle gunmen on Sunday morning, RCN radio reported. It was not immediately clear who was responsible.
Since its formation in 1985, scores of representatives of the Union Patriotica, said to be the FARC's political wing, have been targeted by suspected right-wing paramilitary groups.
